episodes.194262: A shortwave trough moved south from Colorado over New Mexico on September 5th. This combined with upslope surface flow from a backdoor front resulted in the development of showers and storms over the northern mountains moving south and east across lower elevations during the afternoon and evening hours. These showers and storms resulted in some flash flooding over the HPCC burn scar and at Bandelier National Monument along with some large hail and severe thunderstorm wind gusts north of Albuquerque, the East Mountain Communities, and across the White Sands Missile Range. Strong east canyon wind gusts were observed across the Albuquerque Metro and across the White Sands Missile Range in the south central highlands during the evening hours as storm outflow combined with the backdoor front moved through. Showers and storms gradually dissipated across south central New Mexico after sunset.
episodes.194280: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.194281: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.196151: Another wet, unsettled day continued across much of NE FL and coastal SE GA as a surface front draped across north FL lifted slowly northward. Locally, near record high |deep layer moisture with PWAT values 2-2.5 inches were in place with weak steering flow. Waves of morning coastal rainfall expanded inland with diurnal heating.
episodes.196207: A nearly stationary front meandered over NE FL with very high atmospheric moisture with PWATs 2.3-2.6 inches. This forcing and moisture combined with passing short wave troughs aloft and weak mesolows created isolated stronger storms with gusty winds and waves of very heavy, locally flooding rainfall.
episodes.196209: A nearly stationary front meandered over NE FL with very high atmospheric moisture with PWATs 2.3-2.6 inches. This forcing and moisture combined with passing short wave troughs aloft and weak mesolows created isolated stronger storms with gusty winds and waves of very heavy, locally flooding rainfall.
episodes.196403: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the Ohio River during the afternoon hours on September 6th. These showers and storms were aided in development by a warm and humid air mass ahead of a surface cold front which moved through the area during the evening hours. While most of the thunderstorm activity was sub-severe, one or two stronger storms was able to produce isolated wind damage.
episodes.196408: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the Ohio River during the afternoon hours on September 6th. These showers and storms were aided in development by a warm and humid air mass ahead of a surface cold front which moved through the area during the evening hours. While most of the thunderstorm activity was sub-severe, one or two stronger storms was able to produce isolated wind damage.
episodes.196483: A shortwave trough and associated cold front crossed the Upper Ohio Valley during the afternoon and evening hours of September 6th.  Sufficient instability and shear supported a few reports of large hail, but downdraft CAPE values of 1000 to 1200 J/kg were key in the creation of a number of damaging wind gusts with some of the storms. Mainly trees and power poles were affected.
episodes.196484: A shortwave trough and associated cold front crossed the Upper Ohio Valley during the afternoon and evening hours of September 6th.  Sufficient instability and shear supported a few reports of large hail, but downdraft CAPE values of 1000 to 1200 J/kg were key in the creation of several damaging wind gusts in Columbiana and Jefferson Counties.
episodes.196607: On the afternoon of September 6th, a cold front pressing through the Ohio Valley tapped into daytime heating to help create showers and thunderstorms across southeast Ohio. Dry air aloft yielded an environment capable of strong downburst wind gusts, and caused multiple areas of downed trees in Morgan and Athens Counties. Storms then weakened as they traveled east of the Ohio River in response to the loss of daytime heating after sunset.
episodes.196900: An upper level trough dropping from the the Upper Great Lakes toward the Mid-Atlantic region dropped a cold front into eastern Kentucky on the evening of 6th. Though shear and instability were unimpressive, dry air aloft and an inverted V-sounding profile were favorable for the generation of gusty winds. A cluster of more sustained thunderstorms approached the I-64 corridor during the evening hours and generated damaging outflow wind gusts near Owingsville before the parent storms weakened with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.196982: After multiple days of off and on rain from the stalled boundary along the LA coast, more rain in association with that boundary fell across southeast Louisiana. This time, the heaviest rain fell closer to the coast in portions of Terrebonne and St. Charles parish where instances of flash flooding occured.
